title: How Long, O LORD? From Forsakenness to Song
summary: Four times David asks “How long?”: how long will God forget him, hide his face, leave him wrestling with sorrow, and let his enemy win? He asks God to answer and give light to his eyes before he sinks into death. Then, without any change in circumstances reported, he declares his trust in God's loving devotion and promises to sing, because the LORD has been good to him.

line: Four times David asks how long God will forget him, then, with nothing yet changed, sets his trust in God's loving devotion and promises to sing.
guide: Asking how long four times over is not a lack of faith; it is faith arguing with a God it still believes is there. Pray all six verses. If you cannot yet say verse 5 for yourself, say it as the church's words, and let them wait in you until they become your own.

care.text: If ‘sorrow in my heart each day’ (verse 2) is your life now, please do not carry it alone. Tell someone you trust: a doctor, a pastor or a friend. If you have thoughts of hurting yourself, speak to someone today. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Petition: answer me before I sleep in death
Trust and praise: I will sing to the LORD

verses.t: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
How long must I wrestle in my soul, with sorrow in my heart each day? How long will my enemy dominate me?
Consider me and respond, O LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death,
lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him,” and my foes rejoice when I fall.
But I have trusted in Your loving devotion; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, for He has been good to me.
